text:
We confirmed that the Ostrava Lake sediment study came from Brennick University, where a team from the Department of Applied Geoscience finished the core analysis in late September. The group, led by Dr. Mara Velek, pulled 18 sediment columns from the lake bed and used layer-counting plus isotope checks to trace deposition back 340 years. Their report says the oldest intact stratum held the clearest industrial markers, including elevated zinc and soot particles.

- Lead institution: Brennick University
- Lead author: Dr. Mara Velek
- Sampling window: 18–27 September
- Core count: 18
- Core depth: up to 6.4 meters
- Key finding: strongest contamination spike dated to 1912–1931
